rows.rationale: This is a lexeme frequency statistic on both lexeme and word nodes, not a lexical sense, form, or a cross-corpus shared frequency. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The occurrence-frequency integer is attached to word nodes and measures source tokens; it is not a lexical-entry identifier or a semantic relation. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The consonantal transliteration is a word-surface rendering, so its value cannot establish an OntoLex lexical Form identity or a lemma key. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The Hebrew-script consonantal rendering of a word is a written surface representation, not a separate lexical entry or sense. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The pointed-transliterated lexeme realization occurs on word nodes; repeated text by itself is not a persistent Form object. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The pointed Hebrew realization of a lexeme is a representation string on words, not a separately identified lexical Form. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The pointed-transliterated word is token-specific (including reading details); treating it as canonical lexical Form would erase token versus lexeme scope. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

This fully pointed Hebrew word is a token rendering; identical Unicode strings cannot be assumed to identify one source Form. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The original English BHSA gloss repeats on word and lex nodes, without a source LexicalSense, SKOS Concept, or attested reference. A shared translation text does not establish semantic identity; this field is native-only pending sense authority.

The source records Hebrew or Aramaic on word and lexeme nodes; a language label is not a LexicalEntry or a SKOS lexical concept. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The hbo/arc feature values are corpus language metadata on word and lex nodes. OntoLex language annotations require correct entity scope and language-tag policy; never infer lexical identity or common concept from those codes.

BHSA lex is a disambiguated consonantal transliteration available on word and lex nodes, not the lex-node ID. A lexical string can be displayed on a reviewed entry, but it does not by itself instantiate an OntoLex Form or provide its identity.

BHSA lex0 intentionally removes lexeme disambiguation; the inventory has 6,461 distinct lex0 strings versus 8,769 lex strings. Treating lex0 as entry identity would merge distinct source lexemes; preserve it only as a native display/search field.

BHSA lex_utf8 is a Hebrew-script lexical spelling on both lex and word nodes. It may serve as a representation of a separately identified lexical Form after review, but identical text alone cannot supply a Form URI or canonicalForm edge.

The source defines this word-level integer as the number of its lexeme occurrences, not a semantic category or lexical identity. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

BHSA nametype is a source category distinguishing native named-entity types, not a published SKOS concept URI or ConceptScheme. A future categorical ontology alignment needs independently reviewed term definitions; native-only for this snapshot.

The rank integer orders lexemes by frequency in this corpus; it must not become a cross-corpus lexical equivalence or semantic class. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The word occurrence frequency ranking is a corpus-local number, not an entry identity or shared lexical concept. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

BHSA root is a word/lexeme morphological root string, sometimes the literal <unknown>. It has no independent root entity identity or explicit OntoLex Decomp edge; do not convert unknown into a resource or assert a decomposition relation.

The pointed-transliterated vocalized lexeme is a spelling/realization string on lexeme and word nodes, not a new Form identity. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

BHSA voc_lex_utf8 is the pointed Hebrew-script spelling of a lexeme, recorded on lex and word nodes. A writtenRep proposal needs an identified Form and a reviewed entry-form relation; neither follows from the literal alone.

BHSA R-005 observes 9,230 distinct, addressable Text-Fabric nodes of type lex. An identified lex node is a plausible OntoLex LexicalEntry under the published 2016 OntoLex Core definition. Only the native node ID, not its lex/lex0 string, can carry that proposed entry identity; it asserts no sense, concept, form, or cross-corpus equivalence. The OntoLex class requires at least one lexical Form, but an attested BHSA lex-node-to-Form identity/relationship has not yet been established; this class candidate must not be promoted until that condition is reviewed.

The source defines this as word text in ETCBC transcription; it is a token rendering, not a lexical-entry or sense identity. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

The Estrangela-script feature records the word text; a script variant cannot independently create a lexical Form object. Without a verified OntoLex entity identity or ontology property-domain binding, it stays native-only in this proposed release snapshot.

Syriac g_lex carries a transliterated lexical realization on word nodes, not a source LexicalEntry or Form node. Do not infer canonicalForm, cross-language equivalence, or a distinct lexeme object from matching lexical strings.

The original Syriac metadata says the English gloss is not intended for translation purposes. It contains no source sense ID, target lexical entity or relation; mapping it to OntoLex LexicalSense, SKOS Concept or VarTrans translation would be an invention.

R-005 assigns Syriac lex exclusively to word nodes and reports no independently addressable lexeme entity. Identical word-level labels cannot establish an ontolex:LexicalEntry, even as a weaker close identity. Supersede the historical research-only close hypothesis conservatively; retain the literal feature until a reviewed construction rule exists.
